headline: Govt cancels order to keep three books in primary school libraries
summary: The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education revoked a directive requiring schools to stock books on Ziaur Rahman, Khaleda Zia, and Tarique Rahman.
details: The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education has cancelled its order requiring all government primary schools to keep three specific books in their libraries. The decision follows public criticism of the initial directive.
caption:
A government order to stock books on political figures in primary schools has been revoked.

The Ministry of Primary and Mass Education has cancelled its order requiring all government primary schools to keep three specific books in their libraries. The decision follows public criticism of the initial directive.

headline_marked: Nahid Rana's 6-wicket haul: [[Bangladesh lose to Zimbabwe by 25 runs]]
headline: Nahid Rana's 6-wicket haul: Bangladesh lose to Zimbabwe by 25 runs
summary: Despite a record-breaking bowling performance by Nahid Rana, the Tigers fail to chase 142, falling short by 25 runs in Harare.
details: Bangladesh suffered a 25-run defeat against Zimbabwe in the first match of the series in Harare, failing to chase a target of 142 runs.
The match was highlighted by Nahid Rana's career-best bowling, where he claimed 6 wickets for just 21 runs, the best bowling figures for any Bangladeshi bowler in an ODI.
Earlier, Zimbabwe batted first after losing the toss and were bowled out for 141 runs in 36.4 overs. Newman Nyamuri scored the highest for Zimbabwe with 33 runs.
Along with Nahid Rana, Taskin Ahmed took 2 wickets and Mehidy Hasan Miraz took 1 wicket to restrict the opposition.
However, the Bangladeshi batting lineup struggled significantly during the chase. The team was bowled out for 116 runs in 33.1 overs.
Nurul Hasan was the top scorer for Bangladesh with 31 runs, followed by Towhid Hridoy with 25 runs. Captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz contributed 10 runs.
The top order's failure led to the team's collapse, with no other players reaching double digits.
caption:
A record-breaking 6-wicket haul wasn't enough. Bangladesh loses to Zimbabwe by 25 runs.

Bangladesh suffered a 25-run defeat against Zimbabwe in the first match of the series in Harare, failing to chase a target of 142 runs.

The match was highlighted by Nahid Rana's career-best bowling, where he claimed 6 wickets for just 21 runs, the best bowling figures for any Bangladeshi bowler in an ODI.

Earlier, Zimbabwe batted first after losing the toss and were bowled out for 141 runs in 36.4 overs. Newman Nyamuri scored the highest for Zimbabwe with 33 runs.

Along with Nahid Rana, Taskin Ahmed took 2 wickets and Mehidy Hasan Miraz took 1 wicket to restrict the opposition.

However, the Bangladeshi batting lineup struggled significantly during the chase. The team was bowled out for 116 runs in 33.1 overs.

Nurul Hasan was the top scorer for Bangladesh with 31 runs, followed by Towhid Hridoy with 25 runs. Captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz contributed 10 runs.

The top order's failure led to the team's collapse, with no other players reaching double digits.
